## Step 1 — Get Your Databricks Workspace 🚀

**Phase 1: Connectivity** ⏱ ~15-20 min

**Sign up:** [databricks.com/learn/free-edition](https://www.databricks.com/learn/free-edition)

**Find your HOST:**
- Look at your browser URL
- Copy everything up to `.com` (e.g., `dbc-xxxx.cloud.databricks.com`)
- Save as **DATABRICKS_HOST**

::: footer
Databricks + Posit Workshop
:::

---

## Step 1b — Find Your SQL Warehouse & HTTP Path 🏭

**In Databricks UI:**

1. Click **SQL Warehouses** on the left
2. Click your active warehouse
3. Click **Connection details**
4. Copy the **HTTP Path** (e.g., `/sql/1.0/warehouses/xxxxxxxx`)
5. Save as **DATABRICKS_HTTP_PATH**

<div class="tip-box">
💡 Warehouse "Stopped"? Click **Start** (waits ~30 seconds).
</div>

::: footer
Databricks + Posit Workshop
:::

---

## Step 2 — Generate Your Access Token (PAT) 🔐

**In Databricks UI:**

1. Click your **user profile** (top right)
2. Click **Settings** → **Developer**
3. Click **Manage** next to **Access tokens**
4. Click **Generate new token**
5. **Copy immediately** — Databricks never shows it again

<div class="warning-box">
⚠️ **CRITICAL:** Do not lose this token. If a connection hangs for a long time rather than failing fast, double-check this and your HOST before assuming something is broken.
</div>

::: footer
Databricks + Posit Workshop
:::

---

**Phase 2: Environment**

**Fork and clone:**

```
https://github.com/philbowsher/Intro-How-to-Use-Posit-AI-Databricks-For-Healthcare-Data-Science
```

**Open it in Positron.** This is your project folder. Everything goes here.

::: footer
Databricks + Posit Workshop

## Step 3b — Make Sure You Have a `.venv` 🐍

**If you created this as a New Project (File → New Project → Python), skip this — Positron already made one.**

If you opened an existing folder instead:

```bash
python3.14 -m venv .venv
```

Then set Positron's Python interpreter (top-right corner) to `.venv`.

<div class="warning-box">
⚠️ Your `.env` file and both R documents hardcode `.venv/bin/python` — skipping this breaks three things later, not just one. And setting `QUARTO_PYTHON` in `.env` isn't enough on its own — Positron's **Render** button uses whatever interpreter is selected top-right, not `.env`. Set both.
</div>

::: footer
Databricks + Posit Workshop
:::

## Step 4 — Create Your `.env` 🔐

**Ask Posit Assistant:**

> "Create a `.env` file in my project root with fields DATABRICKS_HOST, DATABRICKS_HTTP_PATH, DATABRICKS_TOKEN, and QUARTO_PYTHON=.venv/bin/python. Leave the values blank — I'll fill them in."

**Then open the new `.env` file and type in your real credentials.**

<div class="warning-box">
⚠️ Never commit `.env` — it's already in `.gitignore`.
</div>

::: footer
Databricks + Posit Workshop

## Choose Your Language (decide now) 🐍

**Everything today can be built in Python, or in R using the same Databricks data via `reticulate`.**

- Python is the default path for all four workflows
- R has its own version of Workflows 1–2 (more on this later)
- Same data, same Databricks backend, either way

<div class="tip-box">
💡 If you're an R user, this matters for the next step too — you'll also run `Rscript scripts/check_packages.R`.
</div>

::: footer

## Check Your Packages First ⏱ ~5 min

- Open `scripts/check_packages.py` and run it: `python scripts/check_packages.py`
- Checks everything the workshop needs and installs anything missing, one package at a time
- Also checks your Python version, that `.venv` actually exists, and that Quarto can find your interpreter
- Like the setup script, this is infrastructure — just run it, no prompting

::: footer
Databricks + Posit Workshop
:::

---

## Materialize the Dataset ⏱ ~5 min

- Open `scripts/databricks_setup.py` and run it: `python scripts/databricks_setup.py`
- Connects to your Databricks warehouse, runs the workshop's query, writes `data/waiting_list.parquet`
- Every working document reads from this cache afterward — no repeated live queries
- This is also your connectivity check: if this runs cleanly, your `.env` and warehouse are working

::: footer
Databricks + Posit Workshop
:::

## Workflow 1: new_analysis.qmd 📋 ⏱ ~15 min

**Setup already loads `df` (Hospital, Specialty, Days_Waiting, Priority, Pathway) via the shared `scripts/databricks_helpers.py`.**

> "Using the df DataFrame loaded above, create a Plotly bar chart showing average waiting days by hospital, with a dashed red line at RTT_THRESHOLD (126 days). Use NHS blue (#005EB8) for the bars."

Render it and see your data.

::: footer
Databricks + Posit Workshop
:::

---

## Workflow 2: Dashboard.qmd 📊 ⏱ ~20 min

**Rows are already laid out — KPIs, then two chart rows.**

> "Add 4 KPI value boxes here — Total Referrals, Average Wait Days, Max Wait, and 18-Week Breaches — using the df DataFrame loaded above."

Fill in each row's marker the same way, then render.

::: footer
Databricks + Posit Workshop
:::

---

## Workflow 3: app.py ⚡ ⏱ ~30-35 min

**This one's a bit different — it updates live as you change the filters, so take it slower and build it one piece at a time.**

**Sidebar, KPIs, and charts are marked with comments — build them one at a time, not all at once.**

> "Build the sidebar with filters for Priority and Specialty (dropdowns with an 'All' option), and a checkbox group for Hospital Sites."

> "Add a reactive.calc that filters BASE_DATA by the sidebar inputs, then wire the KPI and chart outputs to it."

Run `source .venv/bin/activate && shiny run app.py` (activating first avoids a "command not found" some students will otherwise hit).

::: footer
Databricks + Posit Workshop
:::

---

## Workflow 4: app_streamlit.py 🎛️ ⏱ ~15-20 min

**A capacity-planning what-if tool — simpler reactivity than Shiny (Streamlit just reruns top-to-bottom).**

> "Add a sidebar slider to adjust the RTT wait target, from 14 to 126 days, defaulting to 126."

> "Add reactive metrics showing breaches at the selected target, the delta vs. the 126-day baseline, and estimated additional FTE using: breaches × 45 / (7.5 × 60 × 5 × 48)."

Run `source .venv/bin/activate && streamlit run app_streamlit.py`.

*If time permits: try the alternate build in `streamlit_app/app.py`, or add a 5th chart to whichever workflow you finished first.*

::: footer
Databricks + Posit Workshop
:::

## R via reticulate ⏱ ~15-20 min (optional path)

**First:** `Rscript scripts/check_packages.R` — installs `reticulate`, `dplyr`, `ggplot2`, `gt` and confirms your `.venv` exists.

**`new_analysis_r.qmd` and `Dashboard_r.qmd` are separate R versions of Workflows 1 and 2** — not the same file mixing both languages, two distinct documents.

> "Using the df data frame loaded above, create a ggplot2 bar chart of average Days_Waiting by Hospital, with a dashed red line at RTT_THRESHOLD."

<div class="tip-box">
💡 Only Workflows 1–2 have an R path. Shiny-for-Python and Streamlit are Python-native web runtimes — there's no meaningful "R via reticulate" version of those.
</div>

## Before You Deploy Anything

There are **two separate, non-interoperable ways** to deploy to Posit Connect — pick one before you start, don't mix them:

- Positron's **Publish button** (UI-driven) — if you start this way, complete it fully
- The `rsconnect-python` package/CLI — ask Posit Assistant to drive this directly if you'd rather it handle deployment

<div class="tip-box">
💡 Deploy whichever version you built — the Python or R rendered HTML output. Same two deploy paths apply either way; the language you picked doesn't change how you publish it.
</div>

Starting one and switching to the other mid-way means redoing authentication from scratch.

::: footer
Databricks + Posit Workshop
:::

---

## Optional: Validate Your Data ⏱ ~5 min if time allows

If you have time, run the ready-made scripts in `validation/` — provided scripts, not something you prompt Assistant to build.

- `validation/validate_data.py` — schema checks (no negative wait times, valid priority/pathway values, required fields present)
- `validation/quality_check.py` — a quick sanity-check summary

## Comparing the Frameworks 🔍

**Reference material.**

| | **Quarto Report** | **Quarto Dashboard** | **Shiny** | **Streamlit** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Output** | HTML/PDF | HTML | Web app | Web app |
| **Interactivity** | Static | Static + Plotly | Fully reactive | Fully reactive |
| **Server needed?** | No | No | Yes | Yes |
| **Best for** | Exec reports | KPI monitoring | Internal tools | What-if tools |
| **Deploy to** | Email | Posit Connect | Posit Connect | Posit Connect |

<div class="tip-box">
💡 Start with Quarto reports to build trust, graduate to Shiny for operational teams, Streamlit for planning conversations.
</div>

::: footer
Databricks + Posit Workshop
:::

## Unity Catalog Governance 🛡️

**Every query is audited at the Databricks layer.**

```python
query = """
SELECT grantee, privilege_type, table_name
FROM system.information_schema.table_privileges
WHERE table_catalog != 'system'
"""
```

**Key point:** Row-level and column-level security are enforced **inside Databricks**. Your Posit apps inherit this automatically.

::: footer
Databricks Unity Catalog · Data Governance & Security
:::
